problem: A curve has parametric equations $x=2\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t),\,y=\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t).$ Given that $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=-\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{cot}⁡(2t),$ calculate $\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}y}{\text{d}{x}^{2}}$ at the point where $t=\frac{\pi }{12}.$

feedback.problem: A curve has parametric equations $x={t}^{4}-5,\,y=4{t}^{5}+2.$ Given that $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=5t,$ calculate $\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}y}{\text{d}{x}^{2}}$ at the point where $t=1.$
feedback.worked_solution:
To compute $\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}y}{\text{d}{x}^{2}},$ we can use the formula

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}y}{\text{d}{x}^{2}} & =\frac{\frac{d}{dt}(\frac{dy}{dx})}{(\frac{dx}{dt})}.\end{aligned}
$$

We're given that $\frac{dy}{dx}=5t,$ and we can calculate $\frac{dx}{dt}$ as follows:

$$
\frac{dx}{dt}=\frac{d}{dt}({t}^{4}-5)=4{t}^{3}.
$$

Substituting into the formula, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}y}{\text{d}{x}^{2}} & =\frac{\frac{d}{dt}(5t)}{4{t}^{3}} \\  & =\frac{5}{4{t}^{3}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we evaluate at $t=1,$ and we get

$$
{\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}y}{\text{d}{x}^{2}}|}_{t=1}=\frac{5}{4(1)^{3}}=\frac{5}{4}.
$$
